message.content:
For any angle \(\theta\),

\[
\csc \theta=\frac1{\sin\theta}=\cot\frac{\theta}{2}-\cot\theta.
\]

So the sum telescopes:

\[
\sum_{k=3}^{2019}\csc(2^k^\circ)
=
\sum_{k=3}^{2019}\left(\cot(2^{k-1}^\circ)-\cot(2^k^\circ)\right)
=
\cot 4^\circ-\cot(2^{2019}^\circ).
\]

Now \(\cot\) has period \(180^\circ\). Since \(2^{12}\equiv 1\pmod{45}\), for \(k\ge 2\),

\[
2^{k+12}\equiv 2^k \pmod{180}.
\]

Also,

\[
2019\equiv 3 \pmod{12},
\]

so

\[
2^{2019}\equiv 2^3=8 \pmod{180}.
\]

Thus

\[
\cot(2^{2019}^\circ)=\cot 8^\circ.
\]

Therefore the sum is

\[
\cot 4^\circ-\cot 8^\circ=\csc 8^\circ.
\]

We need

\[
\sec n^\circ=\csc 8^\circ.
\]

Since

\[
\csc 8^\circ=\sec(90^\circ-8^\circ)=\sec 82^\circ,
\]

we get

\[
n=82.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{82}\).
